guides.title: Opinion essays
guides.recognise: "To what extent do you agree or disagree?" / "Do you agree or disagree?" / "Is this a positive or negative idea?"
structure: Introduction: paraphrase the question and state your position clearly
Body 1: your strongest reason, explained and illustrated
Body 2: a second reason, or a concession followed by your counter-argument
Conclusion: restate your position and summarise the reasons

guides.title: Discussion essays
guides.recognise: "Discuss both these views and give your own opinion."
structure: Introduction: present the two views and signal your opinion
Body 1: the first view, explained fairly
Body 2: the second view, explained fairly
Conclusion: your opinion, with the main reason
linking: I am inclined to believe that

guides.title: Advantages and disadvantages essays
guides.recognise: "What are the advantages and disadvantages?" / "Do the advantages outweigh the disadvantages?"
structure: Introduction: paraphrase
if asked, state which side outweighs
Body 1: main advantages with examples
Body 2: main disadvantages with examples
Conclusion: summarise and give a clear verdict if required

guides.title: Problem and solution essays
guides.recognise: "What problems does this cause? What solutions can you suggest?" / "How can this problem be solved?"
structure: Introduction: introduce the situation
Body 1: two specific problems with consequences
Body 2: matching solutions, with who should act
Conclusion: summarise and evaluate

guides.title: Two-part question essays
guides.recognise: Two direct questions, e.g. "Why is this happening? Is it a positive development?"
structure: Introduction: paraphrase and answer both questions briefly
Body 1: answer question 1 with explanation
Body 2: answer question 2 with explanation
Conclusion: summarise both answers
linking: The main reason for this is

guides.title: Positive or negative development essays
guides.recognise: "Is this a positive or negative development?"
structure: Introduction: paraphrase and state whether it is mainly positive or negative
Body 1: the side you agree with less (briefly)
Body 2: your main side, developed fully
Conclusion: clear judgement
linking: It is therefore a largely positive/negative development

guides.title: Cause and effect essays
guides.recognise: "What are the causes of this? What effects does it have?"
structure: Introduction: introduce the trend
Body 1: two or three main causes
Body 2: the main effects
Conclusion: summarise and, if relevant, comment

guides.title: Cause, problem and solution essays
guides.recognise: "Why is this happening? What problems does it cause? How can it be solved?"
structure: Introduction
Body 1: causes
Body 2: problems
Body 3 (or combined): solutions linked to the causes
Conclusion

prompts.author: QEVRANT editorial (AI-assisted draft)
prompts.title: Grades in primary school
prompts.prompt: Some educators believe that young children should not receive grades at school, only written feedback. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
guidance: State your position clearly in the introduction and keep it consistent.
Give each body paragraph one main reason, explained and supported with an example.
Acknowledge an opposing view briefly and show why yours is stronger.
Conclude by restating your answer to the exact question.
plan: Body 1: grades can create anxiety and comparison at an early age
Body 2: but parents and teachers need clear indicators of progress
Conclusion: feedback first, simple grades later
ideas: Grades motivate some children but discourage others
Written feedback is more informative but takes more teacher time
